routing_note: Scope rule: HIGH/MEDIUM that violate acceptance, turn the gate red, or make a published claim dishonest -> repair; everything else -> debt regardless of severity. R1-R5 meet that bar on the dishonest-claim clause. R6, R7 and R9 are LOW and would normally route to debt, but each is a FALSE STATEMENT written by this diff itself -- R6/R7 inside the human-authorised boilerplate/marker-count item that is this PR's own second deliverable, R9 inside the same ADR-027 section R5 already reopens. Severity says how bad; scope says whose PR, and the answer for all three is this one. Each is a text-only correction with no behavioural surface. Orchestrator routing decision, recorded here rather than left implicit.

findings.claim: The `GIT_SHA` branch of the resolver applies no validation, so the documented override renders non-shas as build labels — the exact lie ADR-027 rules out, and ADR-027's own ruling sentence says validation applies 'at any of those steps'.
findings.evidence: src/sec10k/web/build_id.py:63-65 returns `env[:12]` with no `SHA_RE` check, while `SHA_RE` (:28) gates only the file branch (:37). ADR-027-build-identity.md:5 states 'a value that is not `[0-9a-f]{7,40}` is not a build identity at any of those steps'. Concrete inputs (measured): GIT_SHA='latest' -> '/api/meta' git_sha 'latest'; GIT_SHA='main' -> 'main'; GIT_SHA='$ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA' -> '$ZEABUR_GIT_'; GIT_SHA='a1b2c3d4-dirty' -> 'a1b2c3d4-dir'. These are the same strings NOT_A_SHA (src/repo_hygiene/eval_adapter.py:841-845) declares must resolve to `unknown` when they come from the file. The S2 row is literally titled 'Set GIT_SHA on Zeabur', so an operator setting this variable — including to a `${ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA}` reference that does not expand at runtime — is the realistic input. The eval case cannot catch it: eval_adapter.py:919-921 asserts only 'deadbeefcafe' -> label and ''/'   ' -> unknown, i.e. it pins the unvalidated passthrough as correct.
findings.repro: cd <worktree> && python3 -c "import os,tempfile;from src.sec10k.web.build_id import git_sha;td=tempfile.mkdtemp();print([git_sha(td,{'PATH':os.environ['PATH'],'GIT_SHA':v}) for v in ['latest','main','\$ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA','a1b2c3d4-dirty']])" -> ['latest','main','$ZEABUR_GIT_','a1b2c3d4-dir']
findings.acceptance: `git_sha` applies SHA_RE to the GIT_SHA value too (or ADR-027:5 is narrowed to say validation covers only the file), and `build-identity` grows GIT_SHA=<each NOT_A_SHA value> -> 'unknown' assertions that are watched red against the current code first.

findings.claim: ADR-027 §e and prompts/013 assert that the GIT_DIR leak 'reaches production' and was fixed in the resolver, but the production call path is byte-for-byte as leaky as the code on main — only the eval passes a scrubbed environ.
findings.evidence: src/sec10k/web/app.py:127 calls `git_sha(ROOT)` with no `environ`, so build_id.py:59 falls back to `os.environ` and build_id.py:68 passes `env=dict(os.environ)` — identical inheritance to the deleted `app.py::_git_sha` (git diff main...HEAD app.py, removed lines 273-276, which also inherited the ambient env). ADR-027-build-identity.md:92-95: 'The same leak reaches production ... So `git_sha(root, environ)` resolves entirely within `environ`'; prompts/013-s2-build-identity.md:81-83: 'Corrected: the resolver, not the test.' Measured: with GIT_DIR exported, `git_sha(<empty temp dir>)` returns this repo's HEAD ('ff4e041'), i.e. a sha for a repository that is not the deployed tree. The only caller that passes a clean environ is eval_adapter.py:892, so no case can ever go red on the production path.
findings.acceptance: Either the resolver scrubs GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_COMMON_DIR on the default path (and `build-identity` gains an assertion with GIT_DIR set in the environ handed in, watched red first), or ADR-027 §e and prompts/013 are corrected to say the leak is closed only for callers that pass an explicit environ and the deployed path still inherits it.

findings.claim: Three documents of record publish '16 failures' for the blocked pre-commit run, but the committed artifact they cite as the evidence records 18.
findings.evidence: specs/decisions/ADR-027-build-identity.md:88 ('reported 16 failures'), evals/adversarial/build-identity.json `triage.red_first` ('the FIRST run of this case inside the pre-commit hook reported 16 failures ... That blocked run's report is committed at evals/report/20260822-161040-fast.json'), prompts/013-s2-build-identity.md:74-75 ('16 failures'). The cited file's `build-identity` result has `len(failures) == 18` (16 temp-dir failures plus the two GIT_SHA='   ' / '' ones), score 0.9876543 = 80/81, matching evals/report/history.jsonl ts 20260822-161040.
findings.repro: cd <worktree> && python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('evals/report/20260822-161040-fast.json'));c=[x for x in d['results'] if x['id']=='build-identity'][0];print(len(c['failures']))" -> 18
findings.acceptance: All three occurrences read 18 (or name the exact run they mean), so the published number matches the committed artifact cited alongside it.

findings.claim: ADR-027 §c publishes a four-step precedence table and names `build-identity` as what enforces it, but only the file-vs-GIT_SHA edge is asserted — a resolver that promotes `git rev-parse` above both BUILD_SHA and GIT_SHA leaves the case green.
findings.evidence: The only precedence assertions are eval_adapter.py:913-917 (file beats GIT_SHA) and :934-937 (local dev, run with GIT_SHA=''), and every temp-dir assertion runs where `git rev-parse` cannot succeed, so nothing binds source 3 against sources 1 or 2 (ADR-027-build-identity.md:55-60, 'Enforced by' :7). Mutation applied in-process — `git_sha` reordered to try `git rev-parse --short HEAD` first, then BUILD_SHA, then GIT_SHA — `check_build_identity` returned 0 failures, versus 10 for the naive no-SHA_RE mutation used as a control.
findings.repro: In-process mutation: rebind build_id.git_sha to a git-first resolver, then call eval_adapter.check_build_identity(case) -> 0 failures (control: no-SHA_RE mutation -> 10). Full script in the round-1 review transcript; reproducible from the acceptance below.
findings.acceptance: `build-identity` gains an assertion run inside a real git checkout (a temp `git init` + commit) that a valid BUILD_SHA, and then GIT_SHA, each outrank `git rev-parse`; the git-first mutation above must go red before the case is accepted.

findings.claim: ADR-027 §g asserts that if any build-time assumption is false the failure mode 'is the honest one and not a regression', but `build_command` has failure modes that abort the build rather than resolve to `unknown` — a broken deploy is strictly worse than `build unknown`.
findings.evidence: zbpack.json:6 `"build_command": "printf %s \"$ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA\" > BUILD_SHA"`; ADR-027-build-identity.md:117-122 enumerates only 'absent or empty' outcomes. Measured locally: `sh -uc 'printf %s "$ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA" > BUILD_SHA'` exits 127 and writes no file (a builder running the step under `set -u`), and in a non-writable working directory the same command exits 1 ('Permission denied'). Container builders run such a step as a `RUN` layer where a non-zero exit aborts the image build. I cannot demonstrate Zeabur's builder specifically — that half is undemonstrable from here — but the command's non-zero exits are demonstrated and §g's enumeration does not cover them.
findings.repro: sh -uc 'printf %s "$ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA" > /tmp/BS' ; echo $?   # -> 127, no file. mkdir /tmp/ro && chmod 500 /tmp/ro && (cd /tmp/ro && sh -c 'printf %s abc > BUILD_SHA'; echo $?)   # -> 1
findings.acceptance: Either the command cannot fail the build (`printf %s "${ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA:-}" > BUILD_SHA || true`, with the pinned BUILD_COMMAND string in eval_adapter.py:861 updated to match), or ADR-027 §g adds build-abort to the enumerated failure modes instead of claiming `unknown` is the worst case.

findings.claim: The new boilerplate upgrade-trigger comment states a re-measurement that is false for the population its own trigger clause names: detected chrome in the committed corpus reaches 127 characters, not 35.
findings.evidence: src/sec10k/boilerplate.py:60-64 — 'Re-measured 2026-08-22 (S2), still 35 ... every other fixture tops out at 17' sits directly under a trigger worded over 'detected chrome'. Measured over the committed corpus via `extract_items(..., exclude_boilerplate=True)['boilerplate']`: ge-1994 and ibr-pointer-first 127 chars, ksb-2007 123, ibm-1997 and ibr-security-holders 113, ko-1997 88 (all `edgar_chrome`), then jpm-2024 35 (`running_head`). The 35/17 figures hold only for running_head/page_number kinds. So the trigger's first clause ('detected chrome runs LONGER than the 35-char observation') is already satisfied by six committed fixtures today. Also prompts/013-s2-build-identity.md:101 says 'all 39 fixtures'; evals/fixtures holds 39 directories of which one (`repo_hygiene`) is not a filing — 38 were measurable.
findings.repro: cd <worktree> && python3 -c "from pathlib import Path;from src.sec10k.extract import extract_items;m=[];[m.append((max((len(extract_items(str(f))['normalized_text'][s['start']:s['end']].strip()) for s in extract_items(str(f),exclude_boilerplate=True)['boilerplate']),default=0),d.name)) for d in sorted(Path('evals/fixtures').iterdir()) if d.is_dir() and len(list(d.iterdir()))==1 for f in d.iterdir()];print(sorted(m,reverse=True)[:6])"
findings.acceptance: The comment scopes its 35/17 measurement to the repeat-gated kinds (running_head/page_number) and the trigger clause is worded over the same population, so the trigger is not already satisfied by the committed corpus.

findings.claim: The debt row whose whole purpose is correcting a `ponytail:` marker miscount cites one of the four markers at the wrong line.
findings.evidence: tasks/TODO.md:86 and prompts/013-s2-build-identity.md:92 both give `src/repo_hygiene/eval_adapter.py:698`; the marker is at eval_adapter.py:699 ('# ponytail: whitespace-insensitive but token-exact'). The other three refs check out (boilerplate.py:56, web/app.py:47, css_contrast.py:9), as do the re-based app.py:50 / app.py:211-214 refs.

findings.claim: `build_sha` catches only OSError, so a BUILD_SHA holding non-UTF-8 bytes raises out of `/api/meta` (HTTP 500) instead of resolving to `unknown`.
findings.evidence: src/sec10k/web/build_id.py:33-36 — `read_text()` inside `try/except OSError`; UnicodeDecodeError is a ValueError. Measured: writing b'\xff\xfe abc' to BUILD_SHA and calling `git_sha(root, {'PATH': ...})` raises UnicodeDecodeError, which propagates through app.py:127. NOT_A_SHA (eval_adapter.py:841) claims to cover 'everything a BUILD can hand the runtime that is NOT a build identity' but has no non-UTF-8 member, so no case goes red. Low because a build writing binary into that path is not a realistic input.
findings.repro: cd <worktree> && python3 -c "import os,tempfile,pathlib;from src.sec10k.web import build_id;td=tempfile.mkdtemp();pathlib.Path(td,'BUILD_SHA').write_bytes(b'\xff\xfe abc');print(build_id.git_sha(td,{'PATH':os.environ['PATH']}))" -> UnicodeDecodeError
findings.acceptance: `except (OSError, ValueError)` (or `read_bytes` + decode with errors handled), with a non-UTF-8 member added to NOT_A_SHA and watched red first.

findings.claim: ADR-027 §g's list of unestablished build assumptions omits the one whose failure produces a lie rather than `unknown` — a cached build layer freezing BUILD_SHA at a previous commit's sha, which is exactly the 'real but frozen' outcome the S2 gate forbids; I cannot demonstrate it from here.
findings.evidence: ADR-027-build-identity.md:117-122 enumerates only 'builder sets the variable', 'runs build_command in the directory the runtime serves from', 'carries the file into the run image' — all of which fail closed to `unknown` — and then generalises to 'the failure mode if any of it is false is the honest one'. If the builder caches the `build_command` layer across commits (the value must invalidate the layer for the file to move), BUILD_SHA holds a valid 7-40 hex sha for the previous build, SHA_RE accepts it, and `/api/meta` serves a stale label indistinguishable from a current one — the failure S2's Contents cell calls worse than `build unknown`. No local repro exists; this is why it is LOW.
findings.repro: Not reproducible offline. Detected only by the row's own post-merge gate: `curl -s https://whaleforce-sec10k.zeabur.app/api/meta` before and after pushing a second commit — the sha must MOVE, not merely exist.
findings.acceptance: ADR-027 §g names build-cache staleness as a failure mode that does NOT fail closed, and the post-merge UNRUN gate in tasks/TODO.md keeps its 'must MOVE across two redeploys' wording as the check for it.
